# Best luxury real estate agencies in Sydney

If you're looking for prestige property in Sydney, I'd shortlist agencies based on their strength in the Eastern Suburbs, harbourfront estates, the Lower North Shore and high-end apartments—not just their overall brand recognition.

Sydney's luxury market is highly localised: Mosman is a major market for \$5 million-plus homes, while Bellevue Hill, Vaucluse, Rose Bay and Point Piper are particularly important for ultra-premium properties. ## Which agency should you choose?

| Your priority | Start with |
|--------|--------|
| International buyers and trophy homes | Sydney Sotheby's International Realty |
| Eastern Suburbs prestige sales | TRG or PPD |
| Mosman and Lower North Shore | Belle Property or DiJones |
| Premium brand with broad Sydney coverage | McGrath |
| Boutique service with international positioning | Christie's International Real Estate |




## How I'd make the final decision

Before appointing an agency, interview two or three and ask each for\:

- **Comparable sales\:** Three recent sales in your suburb, ideally at a similar price point and for the same property type.
- **The actual agent\:** Who will lead the campaign and personally negotiate with buyers?
- **Buyer access\:** How many qualified buyers do they already know who would realistically consider your property?
- **Marketing strategy\:** What photography, video, editorial, database marketing and international exposure are included in the fee?
- **Off-market versus public sale\:** Which approach do they recommend, and what evidence supports it?
- **Net proceeds\:** Compare commission, advertising costs, campaign duration and likely sale price—not just the headline commission.

My main advice is to choose the **strongest individual agent for your exact suburb and price bracket**, rather than assuming the most prestigious brand will automatically deliver the best result.

One question that would help me narrow this to a more targeted shortlist: **Are you looking to sell a prestige property, buy one, or appoint an agency to handle a luxury property portfolio?**

search_results.title: Grand home of real estate legend Di Jones sells above guide
search_results.description: A three-bedroom apartment formerly owned by late real estate pioneer Di Jones has sold for $7.7 million, surpassing its guide price by $200,000. Located on level nine of The Residence in Darlinghurst, Sydney, and overlooking Hyde Park, the apartment attracted 167 buyer inquiries, 64 inspections, and competitive bidding from three buyers. The successful sale also marks a relaunch of Kim Jones & Co, led by Di Jones' daughter Kim, who had previously excelled in Byron Bay. Di Jones, who revolutionized Sydney real estate by founding its first female-driven agency in 1992, purchased the property in 2011 for $4 million. The apartment will now serve as a city residence for a couple from Wagga Wagga. Another property tied to Di Jones, a two-bedroom Woollahra unit owned by artist Sally Aurisch, is also drawing interest ahead of its November 10 auction with hopes of fetching $3 million. Despite wider market softening due to higher interest rates and cost-of-living pressures, the auction event hosted by Damien Cooley saw 11 out of 12 properties sold, with several surpassing their reserve prices.

search_results.title: Gold Coast luxury property defies downturn as Sydney buyers move in
search_results.description: Despite a nationwide property downturn that has reverted prices and sales to 2023 levels, the Gold Coast luxury real estate market remains resilient. This strength is attributed to a limited housing supply, robust internal migration, and affluent buyers—particularly from Sydney—seeking better value. Michael Kollosche, managing director of Kollosche, highlights how high-end Gold Coast apartments, priced between $25,000 and $35,000 per square metre, offer better value compared to Sydney's $120,000 per square metre rates. Notable recent sales include an $11.5 million penthouse purchase by a European investor. According to Colliers, Gold Coast property prices have surged 84% since 2021, surpassing Brisbane and Greater Brisbane. Analyst Michael Matusik notes a shift from investment properties to owner-occupied beachfront homes, as the city attracts wealthy buyers post-pandemic. Downsizing among affluent homeowners along Hedges Avenue is driving demand for luxurious, smaller residences in the same prime locations. This demographic shift is shaping a robust, high-end market insulated from broader sectoral declines.

search_results.title: Ray White TMG Luxury launches amid Gold Coast market downturn
search_results.description: Ray White TMG Luxury has launched amid a downturn in the Gold Coast property market, marked by four interest rate hikes, Middle East conflict, and changes to federal property tax policies. Ray White chief economist Nerida Conisbee remarked on the market’s uncertainty, though noting it is currently easier to transact. The launch featured a premium Broadbeach Waters property at 29 Namatjira Court with 95m of river frontage, 533 sq m of luxury living space, and high-end amenities such as a cocktail lounge and riverside pool. Despite a 3% decline in overall Gold Coast property values over the past year, the luxury segment in Broadbeach Waters remains resilient, mirroring stabilizing trends in Sydney’s Eastern suburbs and Melbourne’s South Yarra and Toorak. The event also marked the official unveiling of Ray White TMG Luxury, a new prestige-focused division led by CEO Matt Micallef. Micallef emphasized the division’s goal to provide a specialist approach for high-end buyers and sellers, asserting the Gold Coast's legitimacy as a top-tier luxury market. The luxury brand aims to respond to growing demand with dedicated, high-caliber service.

search_results.title: White Fox Boutique pays $87m for Alexandria warehouse
search_results.description: White Fox Boutique, an Australian online fashion retailer, has acquired a warehouse and distribution facility in Alexandria, near Sydney airport, for $87 million. The 10,238 square meter facility on a 13,140 square meter freehold site will support the brand’s high-demand e-commerce operations, including its regular product drops. The purchase, brokered by Colliers, was from the Hendler family, notable figures in Sydney’s property and sportswear distribution sectors. This acquisition follows White Fox's $70 million purchase of nearby property in Dunning Ave, where their headquarters now include luxurious amenities like a café, gym, podcast studio, and more. Founded by Daniel and Georgia Contos, the company started as an eBay reselling venture and has grown into a $2 billion brand popular among US teenagers. As they face a trademark lawsuit from Adidas, the purchase bolsters their operational capacity and offers future redevelopment potential. The site is strategically valued due to its location near major transport links and the scarcity of industrial land in the area. The Contos couple, also investing heavily in luxury real estate, continue to expand their business and personal portfolio with significant real estate assets in Sydney.

search_results.title: Salesforce Tower: OUE REIT buys Ping An Real Estate's stake
search_results.description: OUE REIT, a Singapore-based real estate investment trust, is set to acquire Ping An Real Estate’s stake in Sydney’s Salesforce Tower for approximately $864 million. This acquisition, reflecting a capitalisation rate of about 5.75%, highlights strong investor confidence amid market concerns over rising bond yields and a saturated lower-end market. Previously, OUE REIT had acquired a 19.9% stake in the tower for $357.2 million, affording it pre-emptive rights to further interests in the building. Co-owners include Lendlease’s Australian Prime Property Fund Commercial and Japan's MEC Global Partners Asia. The site, a prominent feature of Sydney Place at Circular Quay, includes the 180 George Street tower with 53 office floors and major tenants such as Salesforce, JLL, and The Executive Centre. Elsewhere in Sydney, other significant commercial assets are being brought to market, including Dexus and CPP Investment Board’s 60 Castlereagh Street and Brookfield’s partial stake in 52 Goulburn Street. The market is currently displaying a divide between prime properties, which continue to attract interest, and underperforming assets, particularly in areas like Sydney's north shore. Despite geopolitical and financing concerns, robust demand for premium office buildings persists.

items.markdown:
## How I'd make the final decision

Before appointing an agency, interview two or three and ask each for\:

- **Comparable sales\:** Three recent sales in your suburb, ideally at a similar price point and for the same property type.
- **The actual agent\:** Who will lead the campaign and personally negotiate with buyers?
- **Buyer access\:** How many qualified buyers do they already know who would realistically consider your property?
- **Marketing strategy\:** What photography, video, editorial, database marketing and international exposure are included in the fee?
- **Off-market versus public sale\:** Which approach do they recommend, and what evidence supports it?
- **Net proceeds\:** Compare commission, advertising costs, campaign duration and likely sale price—not just the headline commission.

My main advice is to choose the **strongest individual agent for your exact suburb and price bracket**, rather than assuming the most prestigious brand will automatically deliver the best result.

One question that would help me narrow this to a more targeted shortlist: **Are you looking to sell a prestige property, buy one, or appoint an agency to handle a luxury property portfolio?**
